title: Vector Search
oneLine: Find the nearest embeddings to a query, fast, at scale.

paras: Once everything is an embedding, retrieval becomes nearest-neighbor search: find the stored vectors closest to a query vector. Exact search is too slow at scale, so approximate methods (HNSW graphs, IVF, product quantization) trade a little accuracy for orders-of-magnitude speed. It is the backbone of RAG and semantic search.
Retrieve the top-k by similarity, usually cosine:
sections.texNote: Approximate indexes return near-neighbors in sublinear time.

sections.code:
import numpy as np

def search(q, V, k=5):
    sims = V @ q / (np.linalg.norm(V, axis=1) * np.linalg.norm(q))
    return np.argsort(sims)[::-1][:k]
sections.caption: Brute force shown; real systems use ANN indexes.

takeaways: Retrieval over embeddings is nearest-neighbor search.
Approximate indexes trade slight accuracy for big speedups.
It is the retrieval half of RAG.
